div.head: Rect 14
div.ab: [14] Be sceaphyrdan. Sceaphyrdes riht is, þæt he hæbbe twelf nihta [d]ingan to Middanwintra 7 I lamb of geares geogeðe 7 I belflys 7 his heorde meolc VII niht æfter emnihtes dæge 7 blede fulle hweges oððe syringe ealne sumor.

Pastoris ouium rectum est, ut habeat dingiam XII noctium in natali Domini et I agnum de iuuentute hornotina et I belflis (id est timpani uellus) et lac gregis sui VII noctibus ante equinoctium et blede (id est cuppam) plenam mesguii de siringia tota estate.

Be sceap hyrdan . Sceaphyrdes riht is þæt he hæbbe twelf nihta ðingan to middanwintra . 7. i. lamb of geares geogeðe . 7 i belflys . 7 his heorde meolc . vii . niht æfter emnihtes dæge 7 blede fulle hweges oððe syringe ealne sumor .

Be sceaphyrdan Sceaphyrdes riht is þæt he hæbbe twelf nihta dingan to middanwintra, and I lamb of geares geogeðe, and I belflys, and his heorde meolc VII niht æfter emnihtes dæge, and blede fulle hweges oððe syringe ealne sumor.

Von Schafhirten. Des Schafhirten Gebühr ist, dass er den Dung erhalte von den Zwölf Nächten zu Weihnachten [den Dung, den die herrschaftliche Schafherde vom 25. Dec. – 6. Jan. abwirft] und ein Lamm vom Jungvieh des Jahres und ein Glockenflies [Wollfell eines Glockenträgers, Leitschafs] und die Milch seiner Herde 7 Tage lang nach dem Tage der [Herbst-]Nachtgleiche und eine Schale voll Molken oder Buttermilch den ganzen Sommer [täglich].

Of the shepherd. The shepherd's due is that he receive the dung of the Twelve Nights at Christmas [the dung dropped by the lord's flock from 25 December to 6 January] and one lamb of the year's young and one bell-fleece [the fleece of the bell-wether] and the milk of his flock for 7 days after the [autumn] equinox, and a bowl full of whey or buttermilk [daily] all summer.

Concerning the shepherd The shepherd’s right is that he has twelve night’s [worth of] dung at mid-winter, and one lamb from the year’s young, and the fleece of one bell-wether [the lead ram of the flock], and his flock’s milk [for] seven nights after the equinox, and a bowl full of whey or sour milk [for the] entire summer.

Regarding the Shepherd It is the right of the shepherd to have twelve nights’ worth of dung at midwinter, and one lamb from the year’s young, and the fleece of one bellwether, and the flock’s milk for seven nights after the autumn equinox, and a bowlful of whey or buttermilk for the entire summer.
div.note: B reads ‘ði.’; Liebermann prints ‘[d]ingan’ (corrected from the Quadripartitus and Gerefa 9). B's ‘geogeðe’ is corrected from ‘geoðeðe’. The Quadripartitus read ‘ær’ (before) for ‘æfter’. Liebermann compares Rect 16.
